name: Dockerized Elixir Workbench
about: The one source of the house's colours and type. Everything visual that is not a cover reads from here through assets/design/build.py: the console's stylesheet, the diagram skill's profile. Edit this file, run the build; never edit what it generates.

violet.from: the printed board of the covers overlay (assets/covers/overlay.png): Elixir violet

gold.from: the seal (assets/covers/seal.png) and the backs' accent

gold-deep.from: the same gold, deep enough to read on light ground

board-warn.use: a state on the band: waiting for your word

board-bad.use: a state on the band: no connection

selection.use: selected text: a veil of the board over what is under it, never a block

accent.use: the one focal colour: a button, a stamp, a focal node

link.use: HTTP and external edges in diagrams

scroll.use: the scrollbar thumb, on the house's grounds

term.use: terminal ground: what runs and what is read as code. Dark on both grounds until 2026-09-07 (assets/design/fuente-claro.html): it follows the theme now, so a light page reads its code on paper A violet ground on the dark since 2026-10-01 (#2D1D3A, the author's second take of the day; #08010E the first, #120B17 before)

term-ink.use: terminal text: the author's on the dark ground, and on paper the dark's own ground for ink (2026-10-01); Nord's nord4 and nord0 before (2026-09-16)

term-scroll.use: the scrollbar thumb on a terminal ground

term-tint.use: a wash on the terminal ground: a hovered line, a diff's gutter, a hunk's head

svc-compute.use: a service that runs the project's code — the app and its replicas — in logs, events and sessions. The svc-* colours are by ROLE since 2026-09-17, not by service: a cartridge says what its service is for, in the clouds' own words (WorkbenchIgniter.ComposeFile.roles/0), and the console maps the role here (ConsoleWeb.Services) — a service from a cartridge nobody here has seen is drawn without a token of its own. It was svc-app A value a ground since 2026-10-01: the dark's are the ones chosen while the terminal was dark on both, and on paper each keeps its hue and saturation and drops to 4.5:1 (assets/design/palette.py, svc_light) — they read at 2.1 to 3.0:1 there

svc-database.use: a service that keeps the project's data: the role database, and cache, storage and search until one of them needs telling apart

svc-devtools.use: a tool for whoever develops — pgAdmin, Adminer, k6 — and the role identity. It was svc-pgadmin; Adminer had a green of its own

svc-observability.use: what watches the deployment: Prometheus, Grafana. The green Adminer had; these two had no colour at all and fell on the pod's

svc-network.use: what lets traffic in and spreads it — the pod, the pause container that owns the namespace — the role messaging, and any role the console does not know. It was svc-pod

svc-balancer.use: the balancer, in the scaled deployment: the skeleton's own, a network service told apart from the pod

svc-job.use: what runs once and ends: the migration, the one-shots before it. It was svc-migrate

addr-port.use: the layer square on an address that is a service's port, read off docker compose ps (localhost:4001, database:5432); violet since 2026-10-02 — it was the link's blue, which the routes took that day. On the dark ground it is a livelier violet than the routes had (#BE9BDE): that pastel sat too near the page's grey, the house's greys being violet themselves

addr-route.use: the layer square on an address the reader opens and the knock reads by HTTP — a route on the app's port (/dev/mailbox) or a service's web face (pgAdmin's /); the link's blue since 2026-10-02, a door being what the reader opens — it was violet, which the ports took that day

addr-output.use: the layer square on a page a tool of the project wrote on disk (exdoc's doc/, coverage's cover/), served by the console off the workspace, the app up or not; grey, the quietest text's, since 2026-10-02 — it was the terminal's green, a moss that read as good's sea green on the cartridge's dot beside it (a canary yellow was tried the same day and left: 1.1:1 on the light ground). A layer, never a verdict

display.use: the band's lettering: labels, headings, names

text.use: prose, as on the backs of the boxes
